question:
This passage is adapted from Henrik Ibsen's 1899 play When We Dead Awaken (translated by William Archer in 1907). In this scene, Ulfheim is introducing himself to Professor Rubek, a sculptor.

ULFHEIM: I believe I have the honour of addressing no less a person than the great Sculptor Rubek.
PROFESSOR RUBEK: (Nods.) I remember meeting you once or twice—the autumn when I was last at home.
ULFHEIM: That's many years ago, now. And then you weren't so illustrious as I hear you've since become.

Which choice best describes the function of the underlined portion in the text?
option a: It reveals that Professor Rubek first met Ulfheim many years ago.
option b: It emphasizes that Professor Rubek has a distinguished reputation.
option c: It suggests that Ulfheim prefers autumn to spring, summer, or winter.
option d: It indicates that many other sculptors are more famous than Professor Rubek.
subject: Reading and Writing
tags: function of underlined portion, literary text
shortexplanation: Addressing Rubek as "the great Sculptor" and noting how "illustrious" he has become, the underlined portion stresses his distinguished reputation.
longexplanation: The dialogue shows Ulfheim praising Rubek's growing fame, and the underlined portion serves to highlight that Rubek is now a renowned, distinguished sculptor, which matches choice B. Choice A is wrong because the reference to a past meeting comes from Rubek's line, not the underlined portion. Choice C misreads the mention of autumn, which marks time rather than expressing a seasonal preference. Choice D contradicts the passage, since the text elevates Rubek's fame rather than ranking other sculptors above him.

question:
Philosophers observe that many people intuitively feel that, although we generally ought not to lie, some situations may make lying permissible. If that intuition is right and we lack an absolute duty always to tell the truth, then what grounds the objection to lying in the first place? Japa Pallikkathayil has offered one response by appealing to a duty to respect others' agential interests: because holding false beliefs constrains a person's agency, we ought not to interfere with the formation of true beliefs unless doing so prevents a greater constraint on someone's agency or an otherwise impermissible end.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
option a: Pallikkathayil's argument suggests that if we have a duty to respect other people's agential interests and if possession of false beliefs constrains agency, then we have an inviolable duty to speak truthfully.
option b: Pallikkathayil's argument shows that if our intuition that circumstances may make lying permissible is correct, then it is unclear whether there are any grounds for an opposition to lying in the first place.
option c: One potential means of justifying opposition to lying is Pallikkathayil's argument that we have an obligation to respect other people's agency that entails a commitment to truthfulness except in certain circumstances.
option d: Many people have an intuitive sense that lying is permissible in some circumstances but lack a principled way to identify those circumstances, and Pallikkathayil's argument may provide a means of resolving that problem.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The text presents Pallikkathayil's duty-to-respect-agency argument as one way to justify opposing lying while still allowing exceptions in certain cases.
longexplanation: The passage asks what grounds opposition to lying if there is no absolute duty to be truthful, then offers Pallikkathayil's argument that respecting others' agency requires truthfulness except when a greater constraint on agency or an impermissible end is at stake. That is exactly the balance captured by choice C. Choice A is wrong because the passage explicitly denies an inviolable duty to speak truthfully. Choice B mischaracterizes the text, which supplies grounds for opposing lying rather than leaving the matter unresolved. Choice D focuses on identifying permissible circumstances, a side point rather than the main idea, which is the justification for opposing lying at all.

question:
A student is writing a research paper on the history of irrigation in the southwestern United States, placing the creation of Searsville Lake (an artificial body of water built in San Mateo County, California, in 1890) within a broader historical context. The student claims that some irrigation methods still used today in southwestern states such as California, Arizona, and New Mexico descend from techniques that far predate the completion of Searsville Lake.

Which quotation from a historian best supports the student's claim?
option a: "The irrigation system developed by the Hohokam people in what is now central Arizona in the 7th century CE was simple but made use of hydraulic engineering design principles that are still utilized by today's engineers."
option b: "The importance of the development of irrigation infrastructure in the American Southwest today cannot be overstated, since it is the most common means of conveying water for food production."
option c: "In the decades following the Second World War, irrigation of arid areas for agriculture increased to such a degree that it now accounts for roughly 70% of the world's water usage."
option d: "Sprinkler irrigation systems, which were developed in the late 20th century, are a convenient technique of irrigating that makes use of machinery in order to spray water in all directions. Many areas of the Southwestern United States are currently irrigated by this method."
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Choice A shows Hohokam engineering principles from the 7th century CE still used today, directly supporting the claim that modern methods predate the 1890 lake.
longexplanation: The student's claim needs a quotation linking present-day southwestern irrigation to techniques far older than Searsville Lake (1890). Choice A does exactly this, noting that 7th-century Hohokam hydraulic principles are still used by today's engineers. Choice B only stresses the importance of modern irrigation, offering no long lineage. Choice C describes a post-World War II increase, which is more recent than 1890, not earlier. Choice D describes late-20th-century sprinkler systems, again far more recent than the lake, so it undercuts rather than supports the claim.

question:
The subscription economy has grown quickly to cover a wide range of products—from books to cloud storage—partly because consumers value the convenience of automatic payments. But a study led by Ben Klopack and colleagues shows that consumers are typically inattentive to those automatic charges and stay subscribed to services long after their value has faded. The study also found that subscribers were much more likely to cancel a service when they had to make an active renewal decision (for example, when updating payment information was required to stay subscribed) than at other times. The researchers therefore concluded that a regulation requiring all subscribers to complete payments manually would likely _____

Which choice most logically completes the text?
option a: deter attentive consumers from subscribing in the first place but would have little effect on whether inattentive consumers decide to subscribe.
option b: decrease subscribers' valuation of the subscription services at a faster rate than if no such regulation were implemented.
option c: enable dissatisfied subscribers to save more money than they would without such a regulation in place but at the expense of a feature that may have induced them to subscribe initially.
option d: result in reduced average subscription durations, but the overall experience of the longest-subscribing consumers would improve.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Manual payments would force active decisions that let dissatisfied subscribers cancel and save money, but they remove the automatic-payment convenience that first drew consumers in.
longexplanation: The text says active renewal decisions prompt cancellations and that automatic-payment convenience is what attracts subscribers. A manual-payment regulation would therefore help inattentive, no-longer-satisfied subscribers save money by prompting cancellation, while sacrificing the convenience feature that initially induced subscriptions—precisely choice C. Choice A is unsupported, since the text does not distinguish subscribing behavior of attentive versus inattentive consumers in this way. Choice B confuses cancellation likelihood with a change in how subscribers value the service. Choice D wrongly claims the longest-subscribing consumers' experience would improve, which the passage does not indicate.

question:
Many contemporary Indigenous painters practice a distinctly Indigenous mode of abstraction; Linda Lomahaftewa, for instance, often builds her compositions from motifs common in the ceramics and other traditional arts of the Hopi Tribe. By contrast, the leading Indigenous abstract painters of the mid-twentieth century, such as the Kiowa artist TC Cannon, generally aligned their compositional strategies with Abstract Expressionism—a school dominated by European American artists—rather than with traditionally nonrepresentational forms of Indigenous art. Thus, in the case of Cannon's generation, the identification of an abstract painting as Indigenous art tends to _______

Which choice most logically completes the text?
option a: depend not on stylistic details but instead on an awareness of the artist's identity.
option b: place a greater emphasis on the artist's biography than on the aesthetic merit of the painting.
option c: obscure the Indigenous origins of certain motifs associated with Abstract Expressionism.
option d: deny the extent to which cultural identity influences an artist's work.
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Because Cannon's generation used Abstract Expressionist styles rather than Indigenous forms, calling their work Indigenous art must rest on knowing the artist's identity, not on style.
longexplanation: The passage contrasts contemporary painters, whose Indigenous identity shows in their motifs, with Cannon's generation, whose style followed Abstract Expressionism instead of traditional Indigenous forms. For that earlier generation, then, the style itself does not mark the work as Indigenous, so classification depends on awareness of the artist's identity—choice A. Choice B introduces an evaluative comparison to aesthetic merit that the text never makes. Choice C is unsupported, since the passage does not claim motifs are hidden. Choice D contradicts the passage's overall point that cultural identity is central to identifying the work as Indigenous.

question:
In rural Minnesota, ecologist Leroy Walston ran a study to determine whether seeding solar panel fields with wildflowers could bolster pollinator populations in nearby food crops. Walston's findings indicate that—assuming solar panel installers' _______ practice has the potential to increase the number of native bees in crops near solar fields throughout the Midwest by up to 20 percent.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A dash after "cooperation" pairs with the earlier dash to set off the parenthetical "assuming solar panel installers' cooperation," letting the main clause continue.
longexplanation: The sentence opens a parenthetical aside with a dash at "that—assuming," so it must close that aside with a matching dash before the main clause resumes at "this practice." Choice C supplies that closing dash, keeping the pair balanced. Choice A omits punctuation entirely, running the aside into the main clause. Choice B's colon and choice D's comma cannot close a dash-opened parenthetical, so they leave the punctuation mismatched and the sentence structurally unclear.

question:
In closing his essay “What Writers Really Do When They Write,” George Saunders likens the craft of fiction writing to the act of juggling. The author-as-juggler performs a _______ gathering of central themes and tensions, the tossing of these elements into a dynamic narrative, and the catching of the resolutions that emerge.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: A colon after "routine" introduces the list that specifies the three parts of that routine: the gathering, the tossing, and the catching.
longexplanation: The clause before the blank, "The author-as-juggler performs a routine," is complete and is followed by a list explaining what the routine consists of, so a colon is the correct mark—choice D. Choice A's semicolon wrongly joins the clause to a fragment (the list is not an independent clause). Choice C's period breaks the list off from the clause it depends on, and "a routine" would be left dangling. Choice B's comma is too weak to introduce the elaborating list and creates a run-on.

question:
A 2016 study by researchers Andreas Keller and Leslie Vosshall, examining how participants described the odors of various chemical compounds, revealed some similarities between the odor of sample 15 (linoleic acid) and that of sample 18 (propionic acid). The ____ primary descriptors both included “sour”; however, the next most common word used for sample 15 was “decayed,” while that for sample 18 was “musky.”

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: No possession is being shown, so both plural nouns stay apostrophe-free: "samples odors" as simple plurals modifying "primary descriptors."
longexplanation: The sentence refers to more than one sample and more than one odor, and neither noun owns anything, so both should be plain plurals with no apostrophes—choice D. Choice A uses a singular possessive "sample's," which wrongly limits the reference to one sample. Choice B adds needless possessive apostrophes to both words. Choice C's "odors'" marks a possessive that the sentence does not require. Only choice D correctly leaves both plural nouns unpunctuated.

question:
In her work, Ponca artist Julie Buffalohead draws on mythical animal imagery to create fairytale-esque drawings and paintings. Since 1989, Indianapolis's Eiteljorg Museum has celebrated the work of groundbreaking contemporary Native _______ in 2013, it awarded Buffalohead one of its prestigious artist fellowships.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: "Artists" alone ends the first independent clause cleanly so the second clause, "in 2013, it awarded...," stands on its own without a splice or extra connector.
longexplanation: The text contains two independent clauses, and the blank sits at their boundary, so the correct choice ends the first clause without improperly linking it to the second—choice D, "artists." Choice A adds "thus," and choice B adds a comma, each producing a comma splice between the two independent clauses. Choice C's "and" wrongly coordinates "artists" with what follows, distorting the structure. Only choice D keeps the boundary correct, leaving the second clause to begin cleanly.

question:
If an animal can recognize itself in a reflective surface (“the mirror test”), it is considered to have self-awareness. In a recent study, scientists _______ for evidence of self-awareness in snakes, species that rely primarily on olfactory rather than visual processing, adapted the test to foreground smell, modifying the scent trails of North American eastern garter snakes and African ball pythons.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: The main verb of the sentence is "adapted," so the blank needs the participle "searching" to form a modifying phrase, not a second finite verb.
longexplanation: The sentence already has a main verb, "adapted," for the subject "scientists," so the blank must introduce a modifying phrase rather than a competing main verb. The participle "searching" in choice D does this, describing what the scientists were doing when they adapted the test. Choices A, B, and C are all finite verb forms, and each would give the single subject two main verbs with no conjunction, creating a comma splice or run-on. Only choice D preserves a grammatical sentence.

question:
A team of ornithologists documented patterns of conspecific brood parasitism among wood ducks ( Aix sponsa ) in California. The researchers observed several female wood ducks visiting dozens of nesting sites and laying eggs to be incubated by other nesting A. sponsa . Subject 7F64B, _______ visited only a select few nesting sites before laying and incubating her own eggs.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
subject: Reading and Writing
shortexplanation: Subject 7F64B behaves opposite to the parasitic ducks, incubating her own eggs, so "alternatively" signals the contrasting alternative behavior.
longexplanation: The passage describes female wood ducks that spread eggs across many nests for others to incubate, then turns to Subject 7F64B, who visited only a few sites and incubated her own eggs—the opposite behavior. "Alternatively" in choice D captures this contrast between two possible behaviors. Choices A and B ("For example" and "In particular") signal an illustration or narrowing of the parasitic behavior, but 7F64B is not an example of it. Choice C ("similarly") wrongly implies her behavior matches the others', when in fact it differs.
